oil.summary: Crude finished a volatile week on a soft note, with WTI settling around $83.44 (-0.11% on the day, -4.16% on the week) and Brent at $88.29 (-1.57% on the day, -6.46% on the week). The week's selloff looks overdone relative to fundamentals: Hormuz disruption risk persists, VLCC spot rates on the Saudi Arabia-to-China route surged to a record $647,000/day as Gulf barrels finally move but at enormous freight cost. Counter-intuitively, a reported US-brokered partial Hormuz arrangement and a temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions to cap prices weighed on the front end, even as Ukraine drone strikes ignited a fresh fire at Russia's Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl. The Graham bill advancing in the Senate adds a longer-term hawkish sanctions overhang on both Moscow and Tehran. RBOB gasoline cratered 9.93% on the day — the session's standout dislocation.
drivers: Partial Hormuz de-escalation signal and US temporary easing of Russia oil sanctions pressured WTI and Brent lower on the week despite ongoing supply-chain stress
VLCC freight rates hit a record ~$647,000/day on the Saudi-China route, reflecting acute tanker scarcity even as some Gulf oil flows resume
Ukraine drone strike on Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl adds to cumulative damage to Russian refining capacity; Russia reportedly turning to India for refined products

gas.summary: Natural gas markets were led higher by a force majeure extension from QatarEnergy, which has pushed back LNG delivery commitments into November as Hormuz LNG traffic remains constrained. TTF slipped 2.26% on the day to €66.555/MWh but retains a striking +14.39% gain on the month, reflecting the structural premium built in by the Hormuz crisis. Henry Hub was modestly lower at $2.881/MMBtu (-0.89% on the day) but is up nearly 4% on the week, with gas rigs rising per the latest Baker Hughes count even as oil rigs fell by 5. US officials have argued that pipeline alternatives could render the Strait of Hormuz less critical for energy flows, a thesis energy experts publicly dispute.
drivers: QatarEnergy extended its LNG force majeure by several weeks as Hormuz LNG flows remain disrupted, lifting Asian and European benchmark prices on the session
TTF up +14.39% on the month — the Hormuz crisis has structurally repriced European gas risk despite today's modest pullback
Baker Hughes weekly data showed US gas rigs rising even as oil rigs fell, consistent with producers tilting activity toward gas in a higher-price environment

power.summary: EU carbon allowances (EUA) were effectively flat at $78.63 (+0.03% on the day), consolidating a modest +1.22% monthly gain against a backdrop of geopolitical noise. TTF's -2.26% daily pullback to €66.555/MWh, if sustained, would modestly ease gas-fired generation costs in Europe, providing a small downward nudge to power prices at the margin. On the structural side, Amazon announced four new Swedish wind PPA deals, pushing its Scandinavian wind portfolio toward 1 GW — extending a trend of large tech buyers locking in long-dated renewable offtake. Middle East war headlines continue to dominate macro sentiment but provided little direct price impetus to carbon today. Headline flow for this sector was relatively thin beyond the Amazon wind news.
drivers: EU EUA prices nearly unchanged on the day; modest monthly grind higher of +1.22% suggests carbon is not yet pricing in a significant demand shock from the Middle East conflict
TTF daily decline of 2.26% provides marginal relief on gas-fired power generation costs in Europe, though the month-on-month TTF surge of 14.39% keeps structural power cost pressure elevated
Amazon nears 1 GW of Swedish wind capacity via four new PPAs, underscoring continued corporate appetite for long-term renewable offtake in the Nordics
sources: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
